research_brief.month_theme: The Hidden Energy Crisis: Why 'Normal' Labs Miss the Real Problem

related_searches: why am I tired in the afternoon

sources_consulted.key_insight: Most top-ranking articles focus on sleep hygiene — gap opportunity for hormone/metabolic angle
Four-point cortisol testing is trending in functional medicine but underexplained for patients

hero_topic.title: Why Your Afternoon Fatigue Isn't About Sleep
hero_topic.angle: Most content blames sleep — we differentiate by explaining the cortisol curve and metabolic signaling angle that standard labs miss
key_points: Afternoon crashes are usually cortisol/metabolic, not sleep-related
Standard lab ranges mask subclinical hormone issues
Four-point cortisol testing reveals the pattern
Targeted protocols show results in 2-3 weeks

quick_tips.tip: Take a 10-minute walk at 1 PM, before the crash hits
quick_tips.why: Pre-emptive movement blunts the cortisol cliff
Stabilizes blood sugar for 6-8 hours, preventing the 2 PM glucose crash

quick_tips.tip: Track energy at 9 AM, 1 PM, 5 PM for one week
quick_tips.why: Creates a simple cortisol proxy that's more useful than most wearable data

myth_buster.myth: If my bloodwork is 'normal,' my hormones are fine
myth_buster.reality: Standard ranges include unhealthy populations. Optimal is a different target — TSH of 4.0 is 'normal' but most people feel better at 1.5-2.0
myth_buster.source_hint: Functional medicine literature on optimal vs. reference ranges

research_brief.practice_spotlight_suggestion: Announce addition of four-point cortisol curve testing to initial workup

brand_voice_alignment.note: Confident, clear, educational without being preachy. Reads like a knowledgeable friend, not a textbook.
